A verry nice hotel 2 km away from the main road. they let us park for 15'000 ppn. amazing view with a nice pool...we were totally alone and the owner is really nice. shower and toilets next to the pool.
Update 2023: 50k for 2 people no electricity, 70k with electricity, plus 20k to use the pool

Location: 62, Arcabuco, Boyacá, Colombia
Name: Arcabuco
Description: A good Place for one Night on the Way to Tunja. On the end from the Town between Gasstation and Hotel. We had ask in the Hotel. They said us. It's no Problem for one Night. It is a big Parking Lot, also for Big Rigs.

Location: Ruta Del Sol, Puerto Salgar, Cundinamarca, Colombia
Name: Tankstelle an der ruta del sol
Description:
Accommodation at the gas station with surveillance
--
Übernachtungsplatz an der Tankstelle mit Überwachung

Location: Morales, Piendamó, Cauca, Colombia
Name: Ferme familiale Chez Marcelo et Lorena
Description: It's a family farm with the possibility camp , cook , wash the clothes and take a shower..

Location: Cl. 7 #1h-33, Neiva, Huila, Colombia
Name: Hotel Sion Real
Description: NB. Only for cyclists. Simple budget hotel in the middle of the centre. We paid 35k for a big room, where we could store our bikes. Incl. bathroom, TV, good wifi and fans. Neiva is not the most exciting town.

Location: San Francisco-El Pepino, San Francisco, Putumayo, Colombia
Name: Pullout next to building ruin
Description: Level spot with plenty of room to get off the road. We ate lunch here, but would be possible to sleep here also.

Location: Ubaté-Chiquinquirá, Fúquene, Cundinamarca, Colombia
Name: Hato Chips
Description: It is a Restaurant and Shop with Cheese and Joghurts,with a big Parking Lot. We ask if we can stay overnight. No Problem, in the Night patrols the Police. It is a good Place on the Highway 45a on the Way to Bogota. The Restrooms are clean, and open the Night.

Location: Dg 21A #47a-2 a 47a-90, Cartagena, Bolívar, Colombia
Name: Hotel LA Cartagena
Description: Clean, cheap hotel close to port. 35.000 pesos for a single room with quite AC and wifi-bathroom. They don't have parking but the hotel next door let me park my motorcycle to their secure parking.

Location: Puerto Antioquia-Tarazá, Tarazá, Antioquia, Colombia
Name: Hotel Monteverde
Description: Basic hotel with a good price! Paid a basic room with AC for 30.000 COP. And they allowed us to put our bikes inside the room! Has wifi and a restaurant beside the hotel.

Location: Cl. 7 Sur #3-2 a 3-236, Pitalito, Huila, Colombia
Name: Coliseo lot in Pitalito
Description: A large grassy lot between indoor stadium and horse stables - public land. To get in you have to come from the back. Fairly level and quiet, though there is a bar and open air stage. So this place might be noisy on weekends!!! Lots of street lights, too many for our liking...

Location: Ventanas-Valdivia, Valdivia, Antioquia, Colombia
Name: Hotel Diocelina
Description: Paid $25.000 COP for a basic room with fan, tv and private bathroom. Got the room in the next building.. wifi couldn't reach to my room, unfortunately.. but the connection is pretty fast in the main building.. and the shower has low pressure. I had to glue to the wall to get the water 😅

Location: Cl. 12b #8 - 38, Pasto, Nariño, Colombia
Name: Taller Mecánico
Description: Nice people! We had a problem with our VW and they solved it y a few hours. They repair all kind of vehicles.

Location: Unnamed Road, Cartagena, Bolívar, Colombia
Name: Vidagas
Description: If you are willing to wait and can catch a cylinder delivery truck before they go in the yard. They can take your cylinders in and have them filled. The yard will not sell propane or cylinders to the public directly.   Worked fine for us. 1 hour process. At end of this street.

Location: Cl. 5 #13-72 a 13-124, Pereira, Risaralda, Colombia
Name: Movil Play
Description: A place that can fix iPhone's as well as lots of other stuff. Sorted 2 iPhone cameras for us. Good technician and good value. Also sell drones, speakers etc

Location: Cra. 4 #4-1 a 4-87, Salento, Quindío, Colombia
Name: Photocopy and Laminating plus Internet
Description: A great little shop to do photocopying (A4 largest) in colour or black/white. Laminating, computer access, Internet etc. Chap really helpful.

Location: Cl. 11a #15-1 a 15-241, Riohacha, La Guajira, Colombia
Name: hospital, nueva clinica de riohacha
Description:
nueva clínica de riohacha
good hospital for tourists ( European standard). you have to pay in advance 200.000.-COP but the treatment was only 40.000.-COP. the rest of the money you get back. the local hospital on the other side of the street seems to be for free. it is very simple... with our children we preferred the private place.

Location: Cra. 20 #12-72, Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
Name: Taller Walter Bedoya
Description: If you are around Cali in a VW visit this place and ask for Emilio Jimenez at 3116274053. Honest and friendly mechanics whiling to help.

Location: 25, Yarumal, Antioquia, Colombia
Name: Hotel & Restaurant La Gorda
Description: Nice and cheap place to stay. Paid for 28.000 COP for economic room. It has TV, private bathroom & warm water. The owner let us put our bikes in the room.

Location: Las Vegas-Curumani, Curumaní, Cesar, Colombia
Name: al lado del rio
Description:
Very good place next to the river to spend the day, very quiet and nice river to bathe.
--
Muy buen lugar al lado del río para pasar el día, muy tranquilo y lindo el río para bañarse.

Location: Vía San Mateo Guacamayas, Guacamayas, Boyacá, Colombia
Name: Hotel Dona Tere
Description: This place is the cheapest and best accommodation we've found anywhere! It's in the beautiful town of Guayacamas which is full of murals and friendly people. Rooms are 13,000 pp - we thought we had mis-heard but no, that's the price. Rooms are simple and clean with a bathroom as well. We asked to use the kitchen and the lovely owner let us. Parking is on the street, but it's a tiny, safe town and we had no worries parking there. Maybe motos could park inside the courtyard. Best value we've found in all South America

Location: Cra. 5 #31-1 a 31-129, Neiva, Huila, Colombia
Name: Gas Neiva
Description: Propane Gas. We paid more or less 30 COP.

Location: Unnamed Road, Villavieja, Huila, Colombia
Name: Desert view
Description: Nice flat place on the way from Baraya to constellation valley with great views

Location: Yarumal-Llanos de Cuivá, Angostura, Antioquia, Colombia
Name: Hotel La Leticia
Description: Nice and cheap hotel for a night. Paid for 30.000 COP for a double bed with private bathroom and TV. Hot shower and wifi available.

Location: Unnamed Road, Salento, Quindío, Colombia
Name: Salento-Toche
Description: This backroad is absolutely great. From here to Toche you will see a lot of wax palms. This is a nice overnight spot in the forest around 100 meters beside the road. Nobody will see you there from the road.

Location: Cl. 2, Belalcazar, Caldas, Colombia
Name: Monumento Cristo Rey parking, Belancazar
Description:
Parking area just behind and below the monument. Not secure, but out of sight of the road. One entrance has a closed fence, the other is sided by a house. Nobody asked me for parking fees when I entered.  Not quite level.
No facilities, but toilets are at the restaurant at foot of the monument.
The first photo is of the parking area, the second looks up from the area.

After driving 13000 km this road (to and from this carpark), an alternative for road 25, tops my favourite roads. Even though agriculture has changed the original landscape. A windy second gear road all the way up, along the ridge and back down again. Along the ridge great views of the valleys both sides with different shades of green from the pasture fields, coffee and banana trees, other fruit trees broken by colourfull flowers. You can tell that the land owners are doing well by the well maintained good looking houses. Most of which are nicely set in the landscape. To me the road is worth 5 stars. A well paved narrow two lane road.

Location: Uribia-Puerto Bolivar, Uribia, La Guajira, Colombia
Name: Attempted Robbery and Full Robbery
Description:
Just a little heads up for overlanders heading out this way. A few kilometres before we got to the turn off to cabo 2 guys on a motorbike were driving along side us with a gun held up to us. We sped off and tried to get another car to pull over for us but as soon as they did they pulled the gun on them too. At that point both cars turned around and headed back out toward the town. The guys followed for a long time but couldn't keep up with us. I don't want to scare anyone away from this area but maybe it's best to do in convoy. I haven't heard about this happening to anyone else so maybe it was just a once off. The police also said if you're going to drive out this way try to do it early in the morning.

Now the got a Car with Germans, French, Brazilians. See Post below... Convoy highly recommended. Don t stop! Run them over!!

Location: Villavieja, Huila, Colombia
Name: Entry/exit of Valle de Constellationes
Description: This route isn't on open source mapping (yet - Sept '17. 22' update: only the first km available), but it's far nicer than the well-driven Tatacoa route just to the south. This is the access route to the Valle de Constellationes camp site,  but all along here are some amazing wild camp spots. there are a couple of gates to open, but at each one there is a tourist information sign.  You can continue down this track to do a loop onto the main Tatacoa road. Go past the two lodge/campsites to the T-junction at the end, turn right, and it comes out at the eastern end of the Tatacoa desert. We saw one local sedan-car doing this route, but ideally you'd want high clearance. It’s a bit rough in parts, but very beautiful. Well worth the effort for amazing wild camping.

Location: Cra. 91 #46a-2 a 46a-56, Bogotá, Colombia
Name: Dian-Aduana dep. Fiscalizacion
Description:
If you leave your car in Colombia and fly back home, then this is the place you need to visit after you arrive back. We had 90 permit as we entered trough port of Cartegena. Unfortunately this was not enough and as we needed to go back home we parked our car near here to the safe parking lot. As we arrived back the exit date on TIP where 1,5 months overdue. You come here. Its puerta G5. There is nice security lady who will take your fingerprint and tell that you want to visit Dian dep. Fiscalizacion on 3'rd floor. They will let you in. After you arrive to 3'rd floor turn left. Go trough class doors and turn right. After another class door there is a security desk. Hand then your driving license or some other type of document and tell them that you need a extension for your TIP. You will be given green visitors pass and security will escort youbto the right person. Ask for la jefe Yolanda. Shes the very nice and helpful boss lady. Explain why you have overstayed your TIP. Better have a good reason. Family emergency is good enough. They will need to see the car to make a confiscation paper. This is part of the process. You need to write on plane paper your explanation why you have overstayed. All communication and writings have to be done in Spanish. Nobody speaks English here :) After they look at your vehicle and fill all the needed documents they will issue you a fine. Fine is payable at 1 floor bank. Only in cash. The fine is calculated by month. So if you come back 29 days after the date on your final day whats written on your TIP then the fine is prox 640thousand pesos. If you come here 31 days after then its double from that. Dress nice say crazias a lot and you will be done in one day. Come 8:30
Oh, and you will only get 5 days to leave the country. Ecuadorian border is 1000km away. You can enter Colombia again 10 minutes after you have left the country. Another 90 days :)

We had the diagnostic work done and some radiator hoses changed then took our car to Osvarca to get the other repairs done cheaper.... like half the price.

WiFi of hotel (pass hotel2016)

Description:
A very cute apartment in a middle class local neighbourhood in Floridablanca. We spent a week here while our car was being fixed and loved it! Everything is very cheap and convenient nearby.

The place is owned by Olga and her husband who are lovely hosts who live downstairs, and they did everything to make our stay awesome, including inviting us to lunch and letting us use their washing machine. 

The apartment has everything you need including a nice terrace to have your coffee, a kitchen with an oven, study, spacious bedroom and lounge area.

Best value and a warm welcome! 50,000 Cop - whatsapp Olga on: +57 317 2131876 to book!

Close by is a cacao farm and some natural Pools. You could also do some hikes. Take a mototaxi or Jeep to come here and leave your car in the small town 'Bonda'. There is a 24h parking one block before the policestation. We stayed two nights and had a wonderfull stay. Recommended!

Location: Tienda, Las Delicias, La Macarena, Ariari, Meta, Colombia
Name: La Macarena/Cano Cristales
Description:
Enroute to La Macarena/Cano Cristales?  Here you decide which road to take.  If you go straight, it's the road that comes up easy on most OSM maps and on maps.me - it goes through El Jardin (@ 2.172272, -74.274522).  We drove this eastbound. It was 138 km from the Terpel station outside San Vicente to La Macarena.

If you go right here, it's the truck/bus route which is harder to find on maps.  We drove this westbound.  It's about 162 km from La Macarena to the aforementioned Terpel.

Both are dirt/gravel mix, both are tricky when wet and, for both, high clearance is needed.

The more challenging is the first route: 4x4 a definite advantage, and a must if wet (it rains here almost year round -  notice how green it is?) so you're bound to hit bad sections and there are steeper grades.  There are at least two dozen small, narrow bridges, (these bridges do not have railings or overheads though), two of which we had to "rebuild" before crossing.  There are two tolls of 7000 and 10,000 COP each.  Keep your receipts for the return trip.

The trucker route is wider in more sections, has no wooden bridges, you pass through larger villages than other route and there are more gravel-less mud sections but still lots of potential for slipping in the rain with soft "shoulders" especially in the second half. --As of Aug 2023 there are 3 tolls of 5K, 10K, and 10K on this route. --

Here are the waypoints for the truck route from this point heading east to assist in taking this route as we had to force our maps to go this way and were assisted by locals enroute to plan it:
- 2.091888, -74.433853
- 2.062654, -74.366702 (town of La Sombra near here)
- 2.061719, -74.248158
- 1.972012, -74.145249 (El Recreo airport nearby which comes up on maps.me but we saw no actual road to it.....)
- 2.077541, -73.974543
- 2.148418, -73.87913
From here you'll hit a right turn up ahead and that road will take you right to La Macarena.  You could now put in coordinates for your destination in town.

Have fun!  We did; we were two rigs and each had to winch out the other on the challenging road at different points! We are 85" wide so JUST made the narrow bridges. There are a few you could go around through the creek as water was not too deep when we were going.

Didn't stay though as I was passing by early morning. 

Turns out heading south towards San Gil there are several more swimming pools along the same creek, some more might offer camping.

Location: Villa de Leiva, Villa de Leyva, Ricaurte, Boyacá, 154001, Colombia

At that point I followed minor routes to the right (away from the house) to the top with the radio antennas. There are plenty minor trails, easy to get mixed up on the way back so maybe keep a GPS track. 

From the top you get nice views down both sides of the mountain. Hiking time might be 45 min to 1 1/2 h each way, distance 2 miles per GPS 2 miles each way.

 Parking for one bike in a little shop around the corner. Nothing for cars, though the town is small and you could just park in front of police station in the center.

Location: Aipe, Norte, Huila, Colombia

Alternatively you can stop at the piedra pinzada" sign and walk a few hundred meters. However the gate at the sign was closed when we where there.

Location: Armero, 43, Armero, Armero - Guayabal, Norte, Tolima, Colombia
Name: Ruins of Armero
Description:
This is a site of one of the largest disasters in history.

On November 13, 1985, Colombia’s Nevado del Ruiz volcano erupted. The pyroclastic flows melted the glaciers at its summit, triggering a massive lahar (mudflow). Despite being located 50 kilometers from the crater, the town of Armero was engulfed by the lahar, which traveled at a speed of 30 kilometers per hour. Of the town’s 29,000 residents at the time, a staggering 80%, approximately 23,000 people, were buried alive and lost their lives.

The government at the time failed to respond promptly and did not deploy military forces for rescue operations. As a result, rescue efforts were delayed, and many lives were lost. Moreover, experts had issued warnings about the eruption beforehand, but the government ignored them. This tragedy was not only a natural disaster but also a man-made one—a catastrophe shaped by negligence and inaction.

Location: Carrera 48, Perpetuo Socorro, Comuna 10 - La Candelaria, Perímetro Urbano Medellín, Medellín, Valle de Aburrá, Antioquia, 050016, Colombia

We found a free WiFi without password on the parking lot. There are restrooms during the tour, not sure if they are available on request.
You can also buy honey and other things from the monastery.
Btw. the desierto (desert) in the name does not refer to the vegetation but the spiritual aspect

sorry, i ve stayed in better places but for the same price there are other options for sure.

Description: We got lost looking for the campsite next to the lake. We came in on the wrong dirt road which turned into a single track dirt path. As we waited on the side of the road deliberating where to sleep, a moto passed with a local guy and his wife. We explained our situation - lost, don’t feel safe driving at night, need a place to park our rig and camp for the night - he led us to a vacant farmhouse with a large covered area to park, amazing view overlooking the lake and a water faucet with potable rainwater. There are lots of farmhouses in this area with large grassy fields, many with amazing views. I’m sure anyone you ask in the area would help you find a farmhouse to camp next to for the night. This location listed on ioverlander may not be possible again but ask around and I’m sure you’ll find a local willing to let you camp the night in their or a friend’s lot. One of our favorite spots in Colombia, and free!

If you are on a moto heading south the boats leave for Saloa at 6am every hour by memory 20000 peso’s but your bike can’t be to big I have a xr250 which would of been ok but it couldn’t fit because of the back box so I had to drive around through El Banco which is like another hour longer

Location: Paz P Bello, Pueblo Bello, Cesar, Colombia
Name: La Helenita
Description:
This generations-old hacienda converted to hosteria is also the site of the Piedras Azules attraction. It is in need of maintenance and updating, and some work was being done on the restaurant while we were there; it was closed because of that.
Otherwise it is a tranquil site (during the week, at least) with friendly owners. Toilets and showers are in barely ok condition, but the staff kept them clean during our stay. They also opened a room for us to use the shower and toilet there.
Big rigs can enter through the gate, but beware of low-hanging cables (about 2.5m) once inside. The owners told us they will keep renovating the site and reroute the cables. 
We did not use the natural water pool, and we did not hike to the waterfall because the trail was in bad shape after the long rainy season.
One issue for us was two dogs kept in a small hut doubling as a kennel. They slept during the day but were barking and howling several times throughout the night.
The hacienda grows and sells coffee and honey, we bought some of both. They have business connection with Nabusimake.

Location: Laundry Cafe, #70-57, Transversal 39B, Laureles, Comuna 11 - Laureles-Estadio, Perímetro Urbano Medellín, Medellín, Valle de Aburrá, Antioquia, 050031, Colombia

best self-wash laundry in town. Hot wash program. Clean machines
12k cop per load, 12k cop per dryer. Good and fast wifi. Coffee

Location: Riohacha, La Guajira, Colombia

Description: Camping and ecotourism lodge. We found this place by accident in maps me. Nice hosts and a simple clean place. They also have rooms but we camped in our car in their huge parking. They can organize trips to the flamingo sanctuary.20000 to camp for 2 people

Location: Carrera 2A, Cabecera Municipal de Jardín, Jardín, Cabecera Municipal, Jardín, Suroeste, Antioquia, 056050, Colombia
Name: Cueva del Esplendor
Description:
This is the place where you hire the tour to Cueva del esplendor. As it is their private property the only way to go is with them. The tour consists on a 4wd ride to a place where you start to walk. The hike has beautiful views, it’s muddy but they will give you proper boots. Then you get to a Finca where they have food prepared for you, and after, you start walking again down to the cave, always with a guide. They say they will only let enter 50 persons a day to the cave in groups up to 8 or maybe 10 people. 

Price is $55000 cop pp. 
and it is definitely worth it 

The lady (owner) is very kind and she even let us park our van inside her garage as a campsite, with cold shower and clean toilets.

s una perfecta opción cerca a Quimbaya y a Montenegro, así puede disfrutar del "Balsaje por el río la Vieja". Es un sitio hermoso, silencioso y muy seguro. Tiene restaurante típico, piscina y una zona verde amplia y tranquila. Muy recomendado. Cop$15.000 (us$5) por persona desayuno incluído

No car parking but there is a cheap parking nearby. 
Free motorcycle parking at their other hotel 20 metres away

We paid 3000 to park and the guy said we could wild camp for free. There are some level spots. We didn’t camp.

Description:
Small hotel outside Zipaquira.

The room was $20 cop. but didn't use the beds, we slept inside our van. Hot shower and fast Wi-Fi. 
They have a hose and let us fill our water tanks

Location: Fuego Verde, Riohacha, La Guajira, Colombia
Name: Pink Flamingos
Description:
Good place to see flamingos. It is a NP so you have to enter with a guide. We got in with Samir, young relaxed guy. His telephone is +57 310370 7361
From Pericos,  there is a "gate" where you get the guide, they asked $20 cop pp. But we negotiated to $10. We were 3 in our party. 
He came with us inside our van. The road is a bit rough and one part is sandy. No big rigs as the tree branches are too low. Our van is 2wd and had no trouble. 

There are many pink flamingos and you can get closer by walking on the lagoon (50 cm deep) or rent a small boat for $10 cop. The closer they let you to the flamingos is about 50 meters as they get scared easy and they fly.

Location: Cra. 29 #14-1 a 14-63, Pereira, Risaralda, Colombia

We stayed 2 nights for 20,000/ night (included entrance to the falls, parking and camping). Flush toilets no paper, no WiFi, no cell signal for us. No shower, we bathed in the river. No running water, we used the stream. Bring enough potable water for your stay. We really liked it here and the river is fun to swim in. Hiking trail to see the upper falls. (8 pretty well behaved dogs live here, don’t know if they allow your dog)

Also to 10 minutes away by car you will find El Moro waterfalls an incredible place to enjoy the natural and clear water.

The tour is in English and Spanish, if you speak Spanish go for that one. The guy is the son of the owner and is much funnier than the one giving the English tour :).

Location: Calle 2, Villeta, Gualivá, Cundinamarca, Colombia

We have shared rooms, camping and hammocks for you

Location: Cajamarca, Centro, Tolima, Colombia

Description: From here heading south 10 of thousands wax palms. Bumpy road and can be muddy but worth while.

Location: Quebrada Bonita, Jardín, Suroeste, Antioquia, 056050, Colombia

Description: Here you can visit a little tunnel and waterfall. Plenty of little bats you can see up close. Nothing spectacular but only 5k pp, 30min tour

Location: Carrera 18, Sibundoy, Putumayo, 861020, Colombia

Description: Safe parking (lots of space) place with also 4 basic rooms to stay. It's simple but very nice people safe and cheap. 15000 for a room for a single person, 20000 as a couple.

Location: Carrera 8A, Barrancas, La Guajira, Colombia
Name: Plaza/Parque in Barrancas
Description: It was late and the police told us we'd be safe parked-up for the night in this square. A flat area and surprisingly  peaceful, we had a good night's sleep but no facilities here.  If you park in the far north-west corner, the police station is in sight, diagonally across on Calle 9. Free.

Location: Villamaría, Centrosur, Caldas, Colombia
Name: Layby Camping
Description:
In a sheltered spot right at the saddle of a 4,000m pass, with incredible views. 

More of a farmer's field driveway than a layby by big enough for a big rig floor several small.  Little or no road traffic at night.

Location: Santa Rosa de Cabal, Risaralda, 661020, Colombia
Name: Short Hike to Impressive Waterfalls
Description:
You can park in Don Lolo Restaurant's car park (polite to ask if he's around) and take the gravel road down the side of the restaurant.

Continue down and across the bamboo bridge across river, then take 2 rights soon after. From there continue up the gorge - at its worst spots its an easy scramble.

Takes about 45 minutes one way. Take your swimming trunks if you fancy a bracing dip (swim out through the narrow channel if water not too scary).

BTW Don Lolo's was recommended to us by a local - big, good food at decent prices (corriente 9k).

Location: Alto de Daza, Pasto, Centro, Nariño, 520001, Colombia
Name: Cheap Petrol/Gasoline
Description:
If you drive the trampoline road east to west you will find the petrol prices are high at around 9,300 until you reach Mocoa, where they drop to 7,500.

Be careful around holidays as on the 1st Jan there was no petrol in this town!

As you come off the west end of the trampoline you will see the same price, and one garage had petrol. If you can make it a little further to Pasto you will find crazy cheap prices around 6,500.

Location: Calle 14, Comuna 1, Pasto, Centro, Nariño, 520003, Colombia
Name: Frenos las Americas

Location: Diagonal 24, Bruselas, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 130004, Colombia

The answer of the friendly stuff to one of the typical travelers questions was ‘aquí no pasa nada...’. There is a restaurant and there are also rooms to rent. Although there is WiFi, it’s obviously not open for guests or only for office use. Bad Movistar reception.

Name: Parque La Floresta

Location: Cl. 43 #43-2 a 43-160, Barranquilla, Atlántico, Colombia
Name: Hotel San Francisco
Description:
Hotel San Francisco: This is a good hotel, with ac, private and secure parking lot, private bathrooms, really clean and comfortable rooms, free breakfast and the staff are super friendly. It’s around 35U$ for a room for 2, in downtown Barranquilla. It’s worth trying if you are passing by and need to spend a night in town. It’s not the most appealing neighborhood, but good enough for its price/quality. 
Ps: parking lot gate it’s not tall enough for the big rigs.

Location: Mariquita - Victoria, Mariquita, Norte, Tolima, Colombia
Name: Cataratas de Medina
Description:
Walk through the jungle, beautiful river with 2 smalls waterfalls and kind of natural swimming pools, also place to picnic and small bar.
4000PCO pp and 3000PCO for parking. 
Maybe overnight possibilities.

Location: Muelle de Los Pegasos, Avenida Blas de Lezo, Centro, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 472000, Colombia
Name: Antonio, boat driver
Description:
Antonio does boat tours to Rosario Islands and pretty much all destinations near Cartagena. Cheaper to book directly with him than through one of the tour companies in town. Super friendly guy. His boat seats about 10. He has a cooler in the boat so you can bring your own food and drink. You can pick up ice at the spot where he fills his gas. He can also get you snorkel gear.

Phone: 3114292380

Our group paid 1,300,000 COP for a full day trip.

Location: 5 estrellas $, 840, Carrera 7, Mirador Del Bosque, Urbanización los Manzanos, Cajamarca, Centro, Tolima, Colombia
Name: Hotel Hospedaje Cinco Estrellas, Cajamarca
Description: Nice clean hotel just next to the main road in Cajamarca. Rooms with TV, private bathroom (cold water only) and fast wifi. Very friendly staff. Many comedors, panaderias and tiendas around. We've been charged 30.000 COP/night for the room with king bed. They let us take our bicycles to the room.

Location: Sancocho Restaurant, Calle 61, Pedro Salazar, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 130002, Colombia
Name: El Posada Alcatraz
Description: Very friendly family.Clean rooms. Delicious breakfast. Max is passionate about motorcycles. Great alternative to save money just outside of Cartagena. 60,000 for double shared bathroom Inc breakfast. 8000 for taxi to centre. parking available for motorcycles. parking on road for cars, or they can arrange secure parking nearby in local car wash. whilst we were there the family helped us out finding a doctor. highly recommended!

Location: La Isla - Bomba La Isla (Municipio de Pinchiote), Carrera 1 (Desvio Bucaramanga Bogotá y Viceversa), Pinchote, Guanentá, Santander, 684039, Colombia
Name: Gasan/Norgas
Description: We were able to pick up a new small 4.5kg tank to replace the disposable bottles for our stove. $65k cop for the tank deposit and $21k cop for the propane. They sold us the bottle straight from the yard so we didn't need to wait for a truck.

Location: Popayán - Isnos, San José de Isnos, Huila, Colombia
Name: Restaurante y Parador "EL TURISTA"
Description: Restaurante y Parador "EL TURISTA" - (Tent Sitio/casa rodente). Food includes a few different type of fishes and then your typical Colombian plates, it was good. For cyclists and possibly Motos, you can camp on the side of the restaurant under a shelter.

Location: Cra. 35 #51-1 a 51-165, Bucaramanga, Santander, Colombia
Name: Panes Y Tortas Integrales - Name
Description: Good place for fresh baked banana bread as well as fruit bread. They also sell different types of cooking/dressing oils, almonds, and yea basically a bakery worth stopping by if your walking around this part of town.

Location: Ruta del Sol, Aguachica, Gamarra, Cesar, Colombia
Name: Chicharroneria el Mono
Description: Off to the East side of the road there is a restaurant with property along the river. I'm not sure if it's public or private but I asked them for general permission to camp with a tent here. They said it's ok. A few locals were also using the river. It's a quiet place with camping along the river on flat and soft land a bit further past the small rocks.

Location: Hotel Central, Calle 8, Curumaní, Cesar, Colombia
Name: Hotel Central
Description: Nice hotel with a courtyard to sit outside under a roof. Solo I paid 15,000 for a private room as a cyclist. The rates started around 20,000 up to around 40k for larger rooms. Wifi is good, they just needed to reset it once. The attendants are helpful, not the most talkative but helpful. Fans in the rooms.

Location: Lavadero Autocar, Vía a la Costa El Copey - Caracolicito, El Copey, Cesar, Colombia
Name: Restaurante y Hotel
Description: On the northern edge of this small town further away from the truck stops/gas station. The double bed room was 15k for me solo. Not a bad spot for the night. Wouldn't say it's a room especial but it works. On a hot day the raspberry juice hit the spot. Service was good be friendly owner. Behind the hotel seems secure me quiet, if you ask I bet you'd be able to sleep in your rig.

Location: Calle 19, Mahates, Dique, Bolívar, Colombia
Name: Hospedaje
Description: Palenque is the town that was the first liberated town during Spanish rule of slavery. There is a statue commemorating this as well as a plaza where local musicians and dancers perform - I don't know how often but on a Monday when I arrived there was a music performance. Tuesday's also may something going on. I say Tuesdays because that is a day that a tour agency from Cartagena schedules its visit. The locals here are friendly and the hospedaje owner was a relaxed guy. They have a private available and a two bed room plus another room I didn't see into. For the double bed room they normally charge 15k a bed but without really many guests you may be able to work out a deal. This is the type of town where I just enjoyed chilling in the plaza and simple life.

Location: Carrera 18, Arboletes, Urabá, Antioquia, 057820, Colombia
Name: Tres Hammocks Hotel/Restaurant
Description: 20k for a single. Also a dorm room option for probably 10k. Loud tv by another guest in the dorm but she gave me the private for just 15k this day. She also has a restaurant and panadería downstairs. It's a nice place to chill out here a bit away from the much busier downtown area.

Location: Sibundoy, Putumayo, 861020, Colombia
Name: Hostal Rancho de Cleo-Fe
Description: a cabin with an excellent view, in the sibundoy valley

Location: Hostal cancui, Vía Santa Marta - Riohacha, El Trompito, Colinas de Calabazo, Santa Marta, Magdalena, Colombia
Name: Antawara Hostal
Description:
Really nice place with very friendly owners. Good breakfast and nice, clean rooms. The only thing that's a bit disturbing is the main road in front of the complex, which is a bit noisy.
Laundry is no problem, little pool is at the place too.

Location: Cra. 22 #29a-2, Guatape, Guatapé, Antioquia, Colombia
Name: Casa Encuentro Hostel
Description: Super nicely located and made hostel. Many opportunities for activities. Located above the lake. The area is clean and very lovingly decorated. We paid for the triple room 180,000 pesos / night. The very delicious and fresh breakfast is included, coffee and WIFI too.

Location: Vía Campoalegre-Neiva, Rivera, Norte, Huila, Colombia
Name: Los Manguitos
Description:
It's a restaurant and hotel. But behind the pool they also have a camping area. Can use bathrooms and showers of the pool area. Not the cleanest bathrooms but ok. No toilet seat, no paper. 
Very noisy from the 45 but for a night totally ok. paid 20000COP for the tent. Motorcycle can be parked right next to the tent. Slow WiFi around reception area.

Location: Vía Planeta Rica - Buenavista, PLAZA BONITA, Planeta Rica, San Jorge, Córdoba, Colombia
Name: Los manguitos
Description: Here is a very comfortable, clean and beautiful hotel. Next door Juan's restaurant serves very good beef sancochos and carrot juices. We paid 30'000 for a double.

Location: Hato La Primavera, Paz de Ariporo, Casanare, Colombia
Name: Finca El Temblor
Description:
The Finca is abuot 20 km after Paz de Ariporo in Direktion to El Totuma. About 8km after Paz go right after a white fence with blue top. Drive about 9 km than you see on the right side a gate "Beatriz", after about 2km is on the right side a gate white/brown. Open this gate and drive some 100m till you can see the house on the right side. 
The owners, Luis and Teresa are very friendly and helpfull. From Nov. till April there are 126 different typs of birds. Luis and Teresa offer Food. If you want to eat (3 times) ts 50.000 cop incl. camping pP. Without food is 15.000 cop pP. If you want food please call 314 211 2546 Teresa, 312 395 8984 Luis Alberto, or 315 221 5522 Fernando and 321 413 7821 Laura en Bogota. The also do the laundry. A place to relax!
High clearance recommended.

Location: Toche - Cajamarca, Vereda Santa Ana, Cajamarca, Centro, Tolima, Colombia
Name: Roadside waterfall Turnout
Description:
Just a small place beside the road, next to a small waterfall. Probably barely worth mentioning, but there are hardly and options along this route. We stopped in at the one nearer Cajamarca, "Pullout on the road to Toche", but it was really too small for our popup truck camper and very hard to level. 

While this one doesn't have the spectacular view, it's protected from the wind and allows you to pull a bit more off the road. It's big enough for one of just about anything, even big rigs.

Locals very friendly, the area feels very safe.

Location: Cl. 5 #14-2 a 14-64, San Agustín, Huila, Colombia
Name: BiciCafe
Description:
Micro artisan roasters with an awesome handmade breakfast and creative pastry.
High quality coffee and very nice atmosphere. There are cupping sessions and language exchange as well. 

They speak English and German an also have bike tours.

Location: Barbosa-Moniquira, Moniquirá, Boyacá, Colombia
Name: Centro vacacional Recrear Gaia - Finca La Arabia
Description: Swimming pool, camping spot, a couple of cabins. Great place to spend a couple of days by the pool. Away from any roads. Loads of space for camper vans or tents. Including electricity. Downsides are all-day music and all-night street lamp.

Location: Carrera 21, Aguachica, Cesar, 205010, Colombia
Name: el rancho
Description: local food. big plates and not expensive

Location: Coveñas, Morrosquillo, Sucre, Colombia
Name: restaurant beach parking
Description: restaurantes marina has a big parking next to the beach. for 10000 cop you can spend here the night. quiet, friendly people, nice beach. shower on the beach.

Location: Puerto Velero, Colombia
Name: Nautical Valero. Place to kite
Description: Www.Nauticavalero.com. This is a great spot for kite surfing. You can camp in your van but Carlos is not that keen on lots of campers, only wants one or two and charges 40,000COP per night, which is a lot when you can camp in so many beautiful places close by for free or for less at some of the other palapa places     If you do decide to camp they have outside shower, running toilets, no hook up but can use the electricity. Hamaca are 20,000 a night. No WiFi. Restaurant but didn’t use. However, you can turn up, park and kite for free during the day. Or take a kit-surf lesson 120,000 per hour.

Location: Terminal De Carga, Bogotá, Colombia
Name: AIR CARGO PACK  BOG
Description:
CROSSING THE ITSMUS  BY CHARGE PLANE   727-200F
A single rate includes all the transport service of the motorcycle, always on time, between  Panamá and Colombia, Daily flights

Location: Club de la pizza, Avenida del Libertador, Localidad 2 Histórica - Rodrigo de Bastidas, Santa Marta, Magdalena, 470001, Colombia
Name: Lubricantes libertad
Description: Great place to change oil and filter.  Very friendly staff and attentive.  Would definitely come back through here.

Location: Cabaña el pulpito, Vuelta al Cocuy, Güicán, El Cocuy, Gutiérrez, Boyacá, Colombia
Name: Cabañas Púlpito
Description: Dorms and double rooms with private bathes. very basic and rustic, not very clean and I suspect the sheets weren’t clean. We were not comfortable but the location is the closest to the Púlpito del Diablo trailhead. We were told there is no longer camping at the trailhead by the park office and the guide. The señora, super nice, serves really good food and will give you breakfast at 0430 so you can be on the trail early. I recommend you start at 0500, it took us 10 hours and kicked our butts. We both had terrible altitude headaches. We used Jorge Puentes as a guide (120,000 cop, same price for all the guides) he was excellent!  The shower in our room trickled hot water, electrifier, maybe better in other rooms?  Price was 35,000 per person to sleep, 15,000 lunch, 12,000 breakfast. As I said really good hearty food. See pictures of the parking, not much space but they do allow camping and your vehicle might fit. Pretty steep drive up but we did it in our Honda Element.

Location: Los Guaduales 2, Mocoa, Putumayo, 860001, Colombia
Name: Canalendres Waterfall
Description:
Beside the nearly unused quiet dirt road to the Canalendres Waterfalls, there is space for 2-3 cars to park or camp. About 1km from the main road the route splits, left down to a hanging bridge, right to the parking space. There is a good spot to set up a tent after crossing the bridge.
The Canalendres waterfall itself is a nice spot to picnic, shower or play in the water. To go there, it's a 10 min walk, which directly turns left (up stream along the river) after crossing the bridge. Or you can walk straight to another waterfall Hornoyaco.

Location: Oasis Hostel, Calle 2, Viejo San Fernando, Comuna 19, Perímetro Urbano Santiago de Cali, Cali, Sur, Valle del Cauca, 760101, Colombia
Name: Oasis Cali Hostel
Description:
Hostel vibe with the class of a hotel. new and clean, great showers, free breakfast, comfy beds, moto parking, street parking for cars though very safe area with two security gaurds either side of the hostel. close to bars and restaurants. australian owner has a 4x4 and klr650, knows a lot about Cali and Colombia, plenty of contacts for mechanics places to go etc.
 relaxing place, bbq jacuzzi, 2 tv rooms, amazing kitchen. also has a dance studio.

Location: Estadio Agustín Codazzi, Calle 9, Zona Urbana, Mocoa, Putumayo, 860001, Colombia
Name: Free Wifi
Description: Free, fast, very unstable. aside soccer field

Location: Panamericana, El Pinar, Piendamó, Centro, Cauca, 190530, Colombia
Name: Hostal Restaurante Don Renzo
Description:
Hostal has two cabins and 3rooms in the main house. It is also a coffee farm. Price is 35pp including breakfast, which includes coffee picked, toasted and ground from the farm as well as other fruits and bread made here as well. Comes with eggs. Amazing stuff! 

Camping is 10 pp, if you would like breakfast (recommended!!) its 6000 pp. more

Luz Angela is an amazing chef, she prepares lunches and dinners, if you are looking to be spoiled and splurge, depending on the dish its between 18,000-35,000 pp.

There is parking and 2 level spots for rigs. 

Luz Angela undertands italian.

If you are interested in coffee culture, Fernando is more than happy to give a coffee tour. The farm sells coffee as for 12,000 the pound. Luz Angela also sells antipasto. 

We were going to spend a night, ended up staying 4. 

For tourism there is Silvia, indigenous town and market, Coconuco with thermals, and the colonial city of popayan is close.

Location: 25, La Pintada, Suroeste, Antioquia, Colombia
Name: Trucker Stop
Description: The classic trucker stop - level gravel parking lot. Next to a hotel. Restaurant on site with wifi which reaches the van. Cold showers available. Plus table tennis and ping pong - overlander oasis. None of the trucks have sleeping cabins but there was a guard here right next to us all night - please give him a propina and / or eat in the restaurant. Best place is next to the restaurant / hotel, in front of the hedge (guard might direct you in). Felt safe and it’s a good option if you’re getting a little desperate on the road.

Location: Basílica Menor La Inmaculada Concepción, Calle 10; Nariño, Cabecera Municipal de Jardín, Jardín, Cabecera Municipal, Jardín, Suroeste, Antioquia, 056050, Colombia
Name: Cafe Europa - Italian
Description: Best pizza in 6 months traveling! The pizza griega is wonderfull. Take a small one and take albondigas as a starter. Prices are very good, still the same. Wine for 8000, which is unique in Colombia.

Location: Crêpes Chocolate, Carrera 6, Dibulla, La Guajira, 446009, Colombia
Name: Villa Marlen
Description: Halfway between main road and beach, charched 20T per night in the parking lot, showers, toilets, no wifi, shade, no high restriction, room for tents in the back.

Location: Tienda del camino, Mina del Sal, Zipaquirá, Sabana Centro, Cundinamarca, 250252, Colombia
Name: Parking Lot
Description: Near entrance of Cathedral, not level but not to bad, quiet at night because not in town. 5000,- per day, so you pay 10000,- per night, let them know you want to spend the night there.

Location: Mondomo-Pescador, Caldono, Cauca, Colombia
Name: Brisas del Rio Hotel/Hospedaje (by the river Ovejas)
Description:
We found this place just randomly because the next hotel&restaurant mentioned here on iOverlander don't offer accomodation anymore iand also the staff wasn't very friendly. 

Ok, so this place don't have any sign atm but they plan to name it "Brisas del Rio". Owned by Emilse&Rodrige, very friendly and welcoming couple. Their daughter Marly speaks a bit english. We paid 30.000 for double room with private bathroom, very clean, safe and quiet during the night. Unfortunately no wifi. They can make dinner, breakfast, snack for you. And you should definitely try Emilse's "pandebobo"-typical pastry for this region (rings made from yuca, cornmeal and queso).

Location: Play Mar, Carrera 4, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 130002, Colombia
Name: Nativo Kite
Description:
Great kite surfing school. English speaking teachers. 120.000 COP. Per hour. Www.nativokiteschool.com. Also have SUPs for rent, a hobie and if you want you can go out on the paramotors or wakeboard   

They also have accommodation dorm room and privates with/without ac. Www.posadakalea.com. 

Nice beach spot and not far from downtown Cartagena.

Location: El Paisa, Carrera 14, MORALES DUQUE, Santander de Quilichao, Norte, Cauca, Colombia
Name: Hotel Panamericano
Description: Budget hotel in the center of Santander de Quilichao. Paid 30.000 COP for double room, private bathroom, TV, fan. Basic but clean, friendly staff. They have a storage room for bicycles, maybe even motorbike should fit there.

Location: Hotel Julian, Carrera 1, Zarzal, Norte, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
Name: Hospedaje Alimara
Description: Budget hotel right next to Panamericana in the small town La Paila. Paid 25.000 for double room with private bathroom, fan. Safe backyard to leave your bicycle, motorbike. Parking for cars only in a front of building.

Location: Calle 24, Santa Cruz de Mompos, Santa Cruz de Mompóx, Depresión Momposina, Bolívar, Colombia
Name: El Sason de mi pueblo
Description: A great family run restaurante in the north of town. Providing breakfast lunch and dinner. Freddie is the chef. We had fish cooked beautifully over hot coals and grilled pork served with rice and beans and salad.  20,000 cop for two including soup and juice and coffee. Well worth a visit. You have to enter down a passage way from Calle de Medio (Carerra 2) just as the road widens out with a central reservation. If you want to order something special in advance, check out the menu or get a delivery ring Freddie on 314 639 9288. Really popular with the locals

Location: Oriental por los Huesos, Carrera 46, Calle Nueva, Comuna 10 - La Candelaria, Perímetro Urbano Medellín, Medellín, Valle de Aburrá, Antioquia, 050016, Colombia
Name: Toyota OEM parts distributor
Description: OEM parts store for Toyota.  They had spark plugs and wire sets in stock for our '98 Toyota 4Runner (Toyota dealership did not stock parts for imports but gave us the recommendation).  $16k cop per OEM plug and $148k for the three wire set ($230 for OEM) with free delivery to our hostel in Poblado.

Location: La Despensa, Toribío, Norte, Cauca, Colombia
Name: Riverside camp
Description: There are several good wild camping spots aside river along Jambaló-Toribío road, this is the one we choosed. It a ~50m long dead side road with a lot of foot pathes down to the river. In theory you can be seen from road, but all pass by without looking into. The road has nearly no traffic at night, but anyway you can't hear it due to the river noise.

Location: Zoológico de Cali, 14, Carrera 2 Oeste, Santa Teresita, Comuna 2, Perímetro Urbano Santiago de Cali, Cali, Sur, Valle del Cauca, 760101, Colombia
Name: Cali Zoo
Description:
A realy good zoo with at least 100 different animal like lions, tiger, tapier, monkeys, crocodil, birds, ... Most animals have big well looking encolsure. We spend a whole great day here.
Opening 8-18, price 20,8k/p + 7k car park.

Location: Brisas del Rio, Carrera 7, Guamal, Supía, Alto Occidente, Caldas, Colombia
Name: Centro Turistico Brisas del Rio
Description: Turistic Center in Supia, they allow us to park inside, it costs 15 mil cop per vehicle per night, the cost must be settled with the person in charge. The place has all basic facilities and a swiming pool. It has security 24 h, it's a safe place to stay.

Location: Carrera 3, Anserma, Bajo Occidente, Caldas, Colombia
Name: Ecohotel Pensil
Description: Really nice, really clean, hotel/love hotel. Spacious rooms with garage are 40,000 COP, basic room 30,000 COP, sleeping in vehicle was 25,000 COP with access to room for bathroom, TV, etc. You may be able to tent camp or use kitchen. I didn’t ask but they were incredibly accommodating. I highly recommend this place for a stopover if you can’t make it from Medellin to Salento. Coffee included. Allowed dogs, no problem. Let us park in garage to work on vehicle. There were employees patrolling parking lot at night, not gated but very well hidden from road— felt very secure. Other guests were staying here for work and said it was very safe. Only downside is lots of truck traffic on nearby road throughout day and night (highway to Manizales is currently rerouted through here), so bring your earplugs if you’re a light sleeper.

Location: Carrera 3, Anserma, Bajo Occidente, Caldas, Colombia
Name: Ecohotel Pensil
Description: Sleeping in vehicle with full access to a room 25,000 COP. See hotel post for more info.

Location: Santágueda, Palestina, Centrosur, Caldas, 176048, Colombia
Name: Big fancy hotel
Description: Didn’t stay, but looks really nice, awesome drive in from Anserma, multiple hotels in town. Really well kept parks and sidewalks. A lovely detour!

Location: Energy Motos, Calle 76, UPZs Localidad Barrios Unidos, Localidad Barrios Unidos, Bogota, Bogota Capital District - Municipality, 111211, Colombia
Name: Energy Motos
Description: Excellent location to buy tires and tune up your motorcycle. Edward is the owner and speaks good English. He was a mechanical engineer so he can fix pretty much anything.

Location: Terpel EDS Las Flores, Avenida Circunvalar, Puerto Colombia, Atlántico, 080020, Colombia
Name: Oil-Change at Posto Terpel
Description: There is the possibility to change oil and oil filter at the Terpel gas station. 15.000 COP per liter 15W40 from a barrel. Free and good service.

Location: Carrera 20, Barrio Santander, Maicao, La Guajira, Colombia
Name: SOAT
Description: The office is located at the corner of Carrera 20 - Calle 15. Here you can purchase your vehicle insurance for Colombia.

Location: Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 130007, Colombia
Name: beach north of Punta de Canoa
Description: A rough dirt track leads down past a couple of farms to a wild, almost deserted, windswept beach. Friendly guy from one of the houses came to check we were ok. Access track ideally needs high-clearance vehicle. 4x4 would probably be required if wet. No facilities. Free.

Location: DADIS, Calle de la Aguada, Getsemaní, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 472000, Colombia
Name: Fatima - free yellow fever vaccine
Description: bring passports and get free yellow fever vaccine. open daily

Location: 36/18, Vía al Aeropuerto, Barrio 27 de Julio, Montelíbano, San Jorge, Córdoba, Colombia
Name: Airport gate
Description: It is at the dead end of a good totally quiet road in front of the gate of the unused local airport. It has road lights and 24h security at the other side of the fence. At sunrise the local cleaning team had their ~30min daily setup meeting at the road some meters away. The airport stuff let us use the toilet.

Location: Carrera 16A, Torices, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 472000, Colombia
Name: Cartagena friends hostel
Description:
nice new hostel in a quiet neighbourhood. safe parking for the bike or 2 cars. friendly owner. air conditioning and good breakfast included in the morning. 
recommended if you don't mind staying a bit far from the center. still, a pretty quick stroll.

Location: Calle 78, Cartagena, Dique, Bolívar, 130002, Colombia
Name: Attempted Robery, unsafe neighborhood
Description: We had time to kill, so figured we would try and take some public transport to our airbnb while we wait for our van.  It dropped us here.  While trying to get a taxi or an uber, a kid ran up and tried to grab our cell phone.  We chased him off, and some locals helped us to GET OUT.  We were told by police, very bad neighborhood.  Don't drive thru here looking for a camp place. It's not safe.  Stay on the main road.

Location: Sogamoso, Sugamuxi, Boyacá, RAP (Especial) Central, 152210, Colombia
Name: Agua Pura
Description: 8,000 COP for 20 liters of potable water. The owners live upstairs and said they are open everyday, you just have to knock on their door around the side of the building and they will help you. Large parking area with easy access. No height restrictions.

Location: Quimbaya, Valle, Quindío, Colombia
Name: La Divisa Finca Camping
Description:
Beautiful, small coffee finca and "organic, natural, sustainable, biodynamic" farm.  Very friendly, energetic owner Javier and his lovely wife Ana will welcome you with open arms and a cup of coffee.  Javier speaks very clear Spanish and is easy to understand. He says you can camp wherever, but there's plenty of level space for 3 or so rigs right at the entrance. No height restrictions, but narrow road to get there.  No 4x4 required.  Camping was quoted at 10,000 COP p/p.  He does a tour of his finca for 50,000 p/p as well.  His tour is better than visiting any Botanical Garden!  If you do the tour, he might not charge you for camping.  He also sells roasted coffee grown here, 40,000 COP for 500grams.  There is a clean bathroom outside with toilet seat and TP, even soap and a hand towel! Water from the tap (agua de la llave) is not potable, but "boiled you can drink it." Also, the finca has 7 friendly dogs. 
Offers breakfast, if asked day before.

Location: Brio, Vía Sachica-Villa de Leyva, Villa de Leiva, Villa de Leyva, Ricaurte, Boyacá, 154001, Colombia
Name: Bici Ful
Description: Great little bike shop. Henry the owner is super helpful and we managed to get everything we needed for new brake lines, gear cables, inner tubes etc. He is open from 8am everyday except Sunday.

Location: Comuna Ecoturística Cerro de Oro, Manizales, Río Blanco, Manizales, Centrosur, Caldas, 170002, Colombia
Name: Road to Reserva Río Blanco
Description: After a lovely bird watching tour we were unable to return to Manizales because of a water main break. The road was torn up and no one could pass so we turned around and found this spot. It is a turn off to the right as you head towards the reserve just past the bend in the road that crosses the river where there is also a foot bridge. We had a very tranquil night camped right on the river. We couldn’t get out  so just camped and don’t know if it’s permitted by the owner, but it does appear others have camped there too and it is a spot where they get sand. A local did tell us it was ok. Private secluded spot just off the road.

Location: Hotel Bordones, Vía a Bordones, El Salto de Bordones, Isnos, Sur, Huila, Colombia
Name: Near hôtel salto de Bordones.
Description:
Bad way on  10km. Sliding by rainy weather. parking possible before the entrance of the hotel "Salto of bordones" on the way flat. beautiful view and Cascade beautiful. Quiet night. 2 hours to go to the waterfall (go and return).
Mauvais chemin sur 10km. glissant par temps de pluie. Stationnement possible avant l'entrée de l'hôtel "salto de Bordones"sur le chemin plat. Superbe vue et cascade magnifique.
Nuit calme.2 heures de marches aller retour pour aller a la cascade.

Location: Colegio San Juan Bosco, Calle 17, Champagnat, Comuna 2, Pasto, Centro, Nariño, 520003, Colombia
Name: Hotel Atahualpa
Description: Budget hotel just four blocks from the center. Big room with king bed, shared bathroom. Clean, nice staff. 20.000 COP/night. Secured storage for bicycles.

Location: Unnamed Road, Salamina, Caldas, Colombia
Name: Mirador Valle de la Samaria (+campground, restaurant, lodging)
Description: Sendero, restaurante and with lodging coming. You can camp here for 10k pp pn. 8,000 pp to hike the sendero with Don Luis, 1 hour. We didn’t camp so we’re not sure on the facilities. It’s beautiful up here and the tall palms are way cool.

Location: Cl. 18 #6-2 a 6-90, Pasto, Nariño, Colombia
Name: Niko Hotel
Description: Excellent hotel with large parking for small and large vans, quiet and safe. Good location close to the city centre and the Panamerican Way. Hot water, wifi, private bathroom, single room for 2 people COP $60K (US $15). We had breakfast and dinner at our motorhome and stayed 3 nights.

Location: Troncal Central del Norte, Vereda Higueras, Duitama, Tundama, Boyacá, 150461, Colombia

With the reinstallation of the leaf spring they ruined the ABS system and installed the leaf backwards (leaf with an eccentric centre bolt !! ). Had no diagnose equipment for European IVECO's. So better drive to IVECO Ecuador for proper service.

Location: Chez Dominique, Taganga, Santa Marta, Magdalena, 470001, Colombia

Description: Very cool hostel. Lots of breeze and nice people. not a party hostel but it has a bar on the third floor which is a very nice place to hang out, have a beer and watch the sunset. No parking but it seems very secure also because is far from the main area and the bars. still, just few blocks from the beach. friendly staff, dogs and cats. paid 17000 in a dorm with fan. 20000 for AC. I think it s 35000 for a private. one of the cheapest hostel in town for sure.

Location: Funza, Tenjo, Sabana Occidente, Cundinamarca, 250027, Colombia

Description: You can drive from the official parking lot at the Bimbo factory into a dead-end road. The road goes along the fence of the factory and is not marked in maps.me. There are huge grass fields on the other side. Very quiet at night, as you are far away from Ruta 50. Best to drive reverse into the road, as there is no possibility to turn. Good for a night, close to Bogota and free.

Location: Aipe, Norte, Huila, Colombia

Description: There is a paved way leading off Ruta 45 to the Magdalena River. Drive about 200 m and turn right into a small flat area just before the second yellow traffic sign. Very quiet during the night, some bugs around. You can pitch your tent well hidden from the road if you just follow a tiny path behind the trees and hills.

Location: Peregino, Calle 11, Villa de Leiva, Villa de Leyva, Ricaurte, Boyacá, 154001, Colombia

Shared and prívate rooms. 
Owners are very chill and easygoing.

Location: San Francisco, Gualivá, Cundinamarca, 253601, Colombia
Name: Finca Los Pinos, San Francisco
Description:
This place has a grassy camping area and unlevelled  terraced parking, bathrooms and grills. Big rigs will fit. We stayed on a Sunday, it was very quiet. There is a small tienda selling beer, etc. Wifi was very good. Adjacent road has little traffic, almost none at night. 25K pp
On weekends, they may host events, so it’s best to call ahead: (+57)312-315-1598
They also have rooms in a separate lot about 100 m away. Large level parking area there as well, but no outside bathrooms. We did not check out this area.

Spend the night here:

Grassy spot under some trees at the front of a finca. We just ask the owners and they say it was ok to stay one night. 
Beautiful road between Yopal and Orocue. Tropical savannah landscape , we saw a lot of animals: many birds, horses, cows, buffaloes, deers, capybara, turtles and caimans.

Location: Garagoa, Neira, Boyacá, 152860, Colombia
Name: Balneario Canahuay
Description:
This community pool on the outskirts northwest of Garagoa is run by a friendly, local family. It has tent camping areas near the pool. We parked in front of the main building on level ground. Toilets are basic (no seat, no paper) but cleaned daily. The six showers are simple (a pipe) in a communal shower room; there are private booths for changing. There is a small store for beer and such, but you can order-ahead a lunch, and the friendly staff will cook something for you. The soup and empanadas we ate were homemade and very good.
Being a community pool, it can be busy, especially on weekends. Of course, there is music during the day, but at a tolerable volume when local folks use the pool. During the six days we were here, including a weekend, it was always quiet by 7 pm.
We were the only campers during our off-season stay. We paid 10k Pesos per person per night. We did not use the pool. Electricity is available by extension chord; we didn’t need any.
Garagoa has an immense Ceiba tree in the center in its plaza! There is a local market every day, bigger on Thursdays and biggest on Sundays. Do try the Arepas Boyacenses made fresh daily over a charcoal fire.
We used this small town as a base to visit villages in the area; very authentic, tranquil, and enjoyable. We hired a taxi with local driver for a full day. Ask the pool staff for recommendations.
